title: The French Express
subtitle: Hurry, the prophecies need to be delivered—before they come to fruition.

content.text: It was two years ago, or sixteen years hence, depending on which chronicle you follow.
To me, it was as vivid as yesterday. But to young minds like yours, it seemed a kind of chaos unheard of.
We should start from the beginning.
With the war coming to an end, France faced countless possibilities. Its people, weary yet filled with hope, longed for lasting peace.
The economy flourished for a time, and people from all walks of life came to France.

Still, the impacts of war inevitably surfaced. As the wartime factories closed, people struggled to survive. Their hardships gave rise to new demands, and before long, Paris became a swirl of competing ideas.
And just how is this connected to your story?

branch.text: That very much depends on your perspective. If your only interest is in the story itself—not the context—you might think it irrelevant.
But I believe context matters. It keeps you from being thrown off by the details.
That said, neither the economy nor society is our chief concern today. What I share with you now is a story, hearsay really—
You presume correctly. A taxi driver caught up in the whirlpool of ideas that spun within Paris.
A heroine born tied to a fate that promises adventure at the cost of her life, who only ever desired a quiet life in the city she loved.
But fate does not ask for permission.
And when this journey comes to a close, regret will be all that remains.
Sounds like this story doesn't have the happiest of endings.
It ends, as all stories must—whether that end is a happy one. You will soon find out.

content.text: A story about this taxi driver, I presume.

items.text: Street, Paris
Must we really sit here, Adèle? I have had quite enough—strikes and traffic everywhere!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Oh, well, yes, this isn't Versailles, madame. The streets in Le Marais are always a tight squeeze. Besides, we're almost there.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I believe the salon should be right above us, in one of these buildings. The traffic might thin once we're near Place des Vosges.
These streets were never the problem, my dear. Perhaps you'd prefer a client that lets you drive on the boulevards of Saint-Germain-des-Prés instead. Now, did you bring what I asked?
The faint clinking of metal reveals the driver's effort.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Voilà! It survived all the bumps!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I know what you'll say, Madame Félicienne, but I must ask again.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Do we really need to carry these pastries around with us?

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Not at all. Provided you ensure there's always a Ladurée around the corner.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: If only that were in my power, madame. Oh look, we're here, and with time to spare. Great, no need to rush.
By now, she's used to her employer's temperament and knows exactly how to calm her down.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I'll be sure to make some adjustments before tomorrow. Maybe stop by the Champs-Élysées and get those macarons you like before picking you up.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: That will do nicely. Now, shall we go in? You worked hard to find that shortcut. Let's not squander our timeliness.
The remark gives the weary driver just enough motivation. She closes the door and spins around with a proud flourish.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: See? Just like I said from the start—

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: "I know Paris like the back of my hand!"

Thou art the Kingdom and the Power and the Glory.
（ATAH MAKUTH VE-GEBURAH VE-GEDULAH)

Forever. Amen.
(LE-OLAHM AMEN)
Divination Salon
Soft smoke fills the chamber, tinged with frankincense, myrrh, and iris root. Gathered onlookers hold their breath in silence, all eyes fixed on the woman in the center.
She murmurs under her breath as she produces a simple wand, half white and half black, tracing pentagrams in each cardinal direction as she throws open her arms.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: Before me, Raphael. Behind me, Gabriel. At my right hand, Michael. At my left hand, Auriel.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: Before me flames the pentagram. Behind me shines the six-rayed star!
Her deep voice trails off, and the burning incense flares bright like a guiding star in the dim room.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: Shown to me ... This, I see ... The whirlwind in the north, the giant cloud, and the blazing flames ...

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: Through the stifling cloud comes light, a piercing flame, a manifestation of divine wisdom.

items.speaker: Lady Visitor
items.text: And what, madame? What do you see? Do you ...

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: Four angels have answered and four aids given so that I may glimpse the secrets of the Archive of Imagery.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: Your husband is nowhere to be seen. Yet his shadow lingers still in the house.

items.speaker: Lady Visitor
items.text: Yes. Yes! How did you know that?

items.speaker: Lady Visitor
items.text: Sometimes I feel his presence. I ... I see him in that khaki coat.
The woman rushes forward, gripping tightly at the edge of the divination table.

items.speaker: Lady Visitor
items.text: Madame, please! What's happened to him? How do I bring him home?
Adèle frowns. She lowers her voice into a whisper that blends into the other murmurs in the room.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Poor woman. Sounds like her husband's gone missing. Just one of who knows how many others that have lost someone lately.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You know, my friend in the police told me there hasn't been any progress on these cases. If only it were as easy as all this. What do you think she'll tell her?

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: That it's a curse, a demonic possession, or some such nonsense. That's the usual prattle anyway.
The diviner gives a small nod to the pleading woman and turns to face her audience.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: He is bound by a curse—held fast in the claws of a monstrosity!

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: A beast born of no mortal womb, a foul creature of darkness, nurtured by the shadows that cloak this city!

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: The old order has been shattered, yet there has been nothing to take its place. We are without shelter, and the beasts are circling, sniffing, coveting our troubled souls.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: They have awakened from their centuries-long slumber, bringing torment upon us! We have called them forth. We have set loose this horror: the Beasts of Gévaudan!

An ominous pall falls over the room at the sound of its name, like a taboo has been broken. The murmurs stop. Breath stops. The pause holds tension like a breaking dam until gasps pierce through one by one.

items.speaker: Participant I
items.text: So that's what those rumblings were. The shadows have returned!

items.speaker: Participant II
items.text: Maybe that's what happened to my missing workers.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah, bravo, madame. "It's a curse," just as you said! The same old rubbish.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: If curses were half as powerful as people think, my family and I would've been snuffed out long ago.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Spare me the morbid talk, would you? How would I ever get around without my driver?
She throws out the remark, then turns a sharp glance to the diviner on stage.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: I cannot expel the beast. It is beyond my power.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: But I do have some means to sap its strength.
Her apprentice steps up at once, holding out several small items.
A crystal etched with a strange symbol, ink, white candles, and a strip of black silk.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: Our world mirrors the one above, bound in its reflection. All things find their place in the Great Chain of Being.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: Sometimes, powers may be drawn from those higher along the Chain.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: From Saturn, I ask for knowledge and insight. And with its power, I offer you this pendulum. Keep it close, and your husband will find his way home.

items.speaker: Lady Visitor
items.text: Thank you! Thank you, madame! There are no words!
Félicienne's patience lasts only long enough to hear that much.
She rises silently, and Adèle follows close behind.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: I was hoping to hear some insights on arcane study or at least some decent gossip. Had I known it was just some poseur selling tired old charms, I wouldn't have bothered.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: There are still plenty of places in Paris worth a visit! If you're in the mood for fashion, there's the Galeries Lafayette Haussmann. Or for antiques and curiosities, we might try le Marché aux Puces de Saint-Ouen. Something to take your mind off this, erm, "performance."
The crowd surges forward, eager for answers. Though a few, like them, slip quietly out from the scene.
Though it seems unlikely anyone would notice, Adèle still lowers her voice.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Perhaps next time, we could go with my—

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Your hours are paid for. You'll take me wherever I like.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Fine. As you say, madame. I shouldn't overstep.
Her usual approach is anything but foolproof. Félicienne stops mid-step, giving her a half-smile.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: These cheap stunts are just a harmless little diversion. Besides ...

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: I believe I'm not the only one who's taken an interest. How have you been finding Dogme et rituel de la haute magie?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah! How did you know about that? I'm just reading it for fun.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Fun, is it? And what about those red squiggles you circled around every entry about generational curses?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah. How on—Did you go through my things? Oh, come on. Tell me!
Their small commotion draws just enough attention to catch the diviner's eye.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: Madame, please stay just a moment longer.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: I see ... clouds and chains around you ... the bonds of one led astray, shackled by fixation ... I might offer some clarity.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: Come closer so that I may see you better.
Only as every eye in the room turns their way does Adèle realize she is talking to one of them.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Félicienne, I think she's talking to you.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: I'm speaking to you, madame. No need to look about. Please, come forward.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Me?
She looks at Félicienne, who, now quite suddenly intrigued by the scene, nudges her driver forward.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Yes, you, Adèle. Well, don't just stand there. Go on! Show her what's what.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: *sigh* Okay.
Feeling the weight of the gawking crowd, she stands across from the diviner and reaches for the pendulum on the table.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Forgive me, madame, but I have no interest in divination. And I didn't come here for any advice, either.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Frankly, I find it difficult to watch you take advantage of all these people.
She lifts the crystal and holds it up to the candlelight.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Excellent clarity, smooth to the touch. Hmph. A fine crystal at first glance.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But there's something else—the evenness of its hue and that flawless sheen. Nothing is ever this perfect.

items.speaker: Lady Visitor
items.text: Whatever do you mean? But ...

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Let's put it through a little test, shall we?
A small dragon pokes its head out from her sleeve as if on cue.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: By   fire,   what   is   false   is   purged.
Flames flicker, yet the woman feels no heat. Though the once-beautiful crystal has been rendered into dull, broken shards.
The little dragon climbs nimbly onto Adèle's shoulder and tilts its head to receive a gentle pat of approval.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Bravo, Feufeu.
The crowd stirs, and Adèle catches a few gasps of awe with satisfaction.

items.speaker: Lady Visitor
items.text: What have you done to my crystal?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Please, allow me to explain. My name is Adèle Tavernier. Have you heard of us before? Les Taverniers? Famed jewel hunters?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: The arcane skill I just used has been performed by my family for generations. We've recovered and examined all manner of treasures, including the Bourbons' own French Blue.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Fire holds a certain power to reveal the true nature of what it touches. Through fire, we discern falsehood from truth.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Sadly, madame, your crystal failed the test. It holds no wisdom of Saturn, nor any power from the so-called Chain of Being.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But luckily, we exposed it before the coin left your hand, didn't we?

items.speaker: Lady Visitor
items.text: I ... This ...
The lady's gaze darts between the diviner and Adèle before she bolts off the stage.
Adèle turns toward the dumbfounded diviner.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: And you, madame, have given a lovely performance, I have to say. It's almost a shame to bring it to an end.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah, if only you hadn't tried to deceive your client with that fake crystal. Things might have gone quite differently, no? My arcane skill would've spoken volumes about your integrity.
She shrugs toward the audience, each face in the crowd falling somewhere on a spectrum between starstruck and stupefied.
Until at last, applause bursts out. Félicienne claps eagerly along with them.
Adèle gives her an "all good" gesture and smiles. Félicienne replies with a brisk turn of her head.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: This is close enough, close enough for me to clearly see the shadow upon you.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Pardon?
She looks toward the diviner and meets those unblinking eyes staring straight at her.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: A Tavernier girl ... The youngest and brightest, brimming with vitality.
The diviner leans forward. The space between them closes too fast. A chill runs down Adèle's spine.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: The fated one has stepped onto her path. Twice will she collide with destiny—once risen, once descended. For a fate left vacant now shall be fulfilled!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You—

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: The call must be answered! Walk with the wise, but beware their words. Beware the gaping abyss of death.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: What lies below shall reflect what lies above—one shall ascend, but all must be paid.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: All must return! All must restore—

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: Monster! ... B-Beast!

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: Urh—Ugh!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: She needs help! Someone fetch-fetch a doctor! Madame, can you hear me?

items.speaker: Participant I
items.text: Why can't she breathe?

items.speaker: Participant II
items.text: What's going on? Are we in danger?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Wait ...

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Is she smiling?
